description: The B5G Network Planning Algorithms codebase compares network-deployment choices for radio-access and optical X-haul systems. It includes a greedy starting-solution notebook, graph-encoded genetic algorithms with and without Steiner mutations, a binary genetic algorithm, local search and CPLEX shortest-path and full-graph models. Input comes from the same repository’s small or full JSON benchmarks for units, roads, paths and demand points. The code produces candidate deployment configurations, cost or coverage metrics and experiment logs. The project places the example network in a region of rural Australia; the model itself has no observational time series. Public GitHub code is free under GPL-3.0, but the IBM CPLEX solver has separate access and cost terms. A telecom modeller could compare heuristic and exact optimization for capacity-constrained deployment scenarios. Some guide filenames differ from the actual tree, and this review did not run any algorithm or solver. Related resources are the separate benchmark-input draft and the project’s standalone dataset generator.
